author: The Current
description:
Chris Thile talks about what he hears when encountering different aesthetics of music
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

How is Chris Thile able to jump so easily from genre to genre? Maybe it’s because he doesn’t see (or hear) it that way. “It just doesn't sound that different to me,” Thile says. “It rarely has anything to do with the aesthetic of it, like what instruments it's being played on, for instance. That's like the cover of the book to me, or the color of someone's hair. [But] what are they actually doing with the materials of music? That's what's interesting to me.”

Hear more of what Thile has to say in this video from his interview with The Current’s Jessica Paxton. On Friday and Saturday, July 31 and Aug. 1, Thile and the Minnesota Orchestra will perform Thile's work, "ATTENTION! A narrative song cycle for extroverted mandolinist and orchestra," a piece of music that captures Thile's encounter with the late Carrie Fisher — yep,
title: Chris Thile on how he hears music genres ... or doesn't

author: The Current
description:
From a 2007 interview, Glen Hansard talks how he was cast in the 1991 film, "The Commitments"
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

In 2007, the late Glen Hansard visited The Current with his band, The Frames. During the interview portion of the studio session, Hansard told the story of how he ended up accidentally being cast in the 1991 film, "The Commitments," about a soul band from Dublin. "I've got red hair, I'm from the Northside of the city, I play guitar," Hansard says, "which fit the bill of the character they were looking for."

Hansard, the Irish singer who won an Oscar for the musical movie "Once" and the led the bands The Frames and The Swell Season, died on Wednesday, July 29, 2026, in a motorcycle crash in Dublin. He was 56 years old.

author: The Current
description:
Stephen Wilson Jr. reflects on his songwriting influences and on his career so far
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

Singer-songwriter Stephen Wilson Jr. grew up in southern Indiana, where he was strongly influenced by classic country artists, including George Jones and Johnny Cash. But he was also inspired by the Seattle sound. "I got massively influenced by grunge music," Wilson Jr. says.

In this interview with Zach McCormick on The Current, Wilson Jr. reflects on those early influences in his life and how they continue to show up in his work to this day — including a song by Pixies that informed Wilson Jr.'s songwriting on his new single, "Hardwired."

Watch the complete interview to learn more about key moments in Wilson Jr.'s life as a person and as an artist — including the event that catalyzed his love of grunge, his rediscovery of guitar thanks to learning about alternative tunings, and about the accident that affected his approach
title: Interview: Stephen Wilson Jr. talks about his many influences and about his career so far

"I got massively influenced by grunge music," says singer-songwriter Stephen Wilson Jr. in describing the event that catalyzed his love of the genre. The music continues to influence Wilson Jr. to this day. 

Stephen Wilson Jr. was Zach McCormick's guest on The Current's July 31, 2026, episode of Tonal Recall, the show that celebrates the music and culture of the 1990s. Listen Fridays at noon Central.
